seats.name: single
argv:
The lib/ directory contains eight small utility functions, one per file. README.md documents the exact required behavior of each. Some of the functions do not behave as documented. Find every discrepancy between the code in lib/ and README.md and fix the code (not the README). Keep each function's name, signature and file location.

Modify the files under lib/ in this workspace; a chat answer alone is not a submitted code repair. Use no network or dependencies. The evaluator runs private tests against your code after completion.

Modify the relevant source file(s) in your current working directory directly to implement the fix described above. Your edit to the existing file(s) is the submission; do not create any other output file.
seats.text:
I fixed all eight functions in `lib/` to match the README. I haven't run any code or tests, only re-read the edited lines.

- **`slugify`**: a run of non-alphanumeric characters now collapses to a single `-`. Before, each character became its own `-`.
- **`chunk`**: the last shorter chunk is now kept. The old loop dropped the remainder.
- **`median`**: it now sorts numerically on a copy. The old code used the default string sort and modified the input array.
- **`formatBytes`**: exactly 1024 now gives `1 KB` instead of `1024 B`. Values below 1024 are rounded to a whole number, which is my reading of "whole number".
- **`parseBool`**: it now trims whitespace and accepts `on` and `off`.
- **`daysBetween`**: the result is now negative when `b` is before `a`. The old code returned the absolute value.
- **`dedupe`**: I rewrote it with a `Set`, which uses SameValueZero as documented. The old `indexOf` version never matched `NaN` to `NaN`.
- **`wrapText`**: the line-length check now counts the space between words, so lines no longer exceed `width`.
